messages.subject: Re: Access to raw (unparsed) POST body?
parts:
On Mar 4, 6:49 pm, Jon <jdgaf...@gmail.com> wrote:
> I'm creating a simple RESTful web api where CSV data is POSTed to an R
> handler.  Data is not form encoded.  Is there a way to access the raw
> POST body for parsing into a data frame?

Absolutely! When you write your R handler, just don't ever reference
the POST variable and instead use a function like readLines() to read
from stdin().

Jeff

On Thu, Mar 4, 2010 at 10:36 PM, Jon <jdga...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Thanks for your rapid reply Jeff.  BTW, I am using the VMWare app to
> get started - excellent idea and much appreciated!
>
> Unfortunately, readLines() is not behaving as I expected. In the
> script below, I consistently get the response "chr(0)" regardless of
> the input I submit, even though the POST variable will successfully
> parse the submitted data when uncommented.

Ah yes... when using the default form encoding type of
"application/x-www-form-urlencoded", the browser sends one line of
POST payload without an end of line marker. In that case you'll need
to ad a bit of extra R coding to capture the incomplete line:

lns <- readLines()
if (pushBackLength(stdin()) > 0){
incomplete_ln <- unlist(scan(what='list',sep="\n",quiet=TRUE))
lns <- c(lns,incomplete_ln)
}

But that bit of code should be used regardless of the enctype, I
think, especially if you're going to post lines of input of CSV, JSON,
XML, etc.

Jeff
